title: Viniyoga of ā satyena

words.gram: the mantra’s first words, quoted as a name

words.meaning: thus; marks the words before it as a quotation
triṣṭubh, the metre of four lines of eleven syllables
in the upasthāna of the Sun

words.role: what the mantra is used for

translation.literal: Of the mantra “ā satyena”: Hiraṇyagarbha the seer, triṣṭubh the metre, Savitṛ the deity, the use in the upasthāna of Āditya.
translation.readable: Ā satyena: seer Hiraṇyagarbha, metre triṣṭubh, deity Savitṛ; used for the midday upasthāna of the Sun.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga leaves two vowels side by side across a phrase boundary of the formula, without joining them.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: ā satyena rajasā (TS 3.4.11.2; RV 1.35.2), the first of the midday upasthāna mantras. The prayoga names Hiraṇyagarbha as the seer; in the Ṛgveda the hymn is given to Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa, which this witness does not mention. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form, so the comma is written with the word in the padaccheda.
in_the_rite: Midday service, step surya-upasthana, before ā satyena (M only).

flags.text: The note that the Ṛgveda tradition gives RV 1.35 to Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa is from the Anukramaṇī, which is not among this edition’s sources; it should be verified or removed before review.
